panels.title: Requests/sec
panels.description: All media requests served by the worker.

panels.title: 5xx ratio
panels.description: Server errors as a share of all requests.

panels.title: p95 latency
panels.description: 95th percentile across all endpoints.

panels.title: Bytes served/sec
panels.description: Response body bytes written across all endpoints.

panels.title: Token cache
panels.description: Access token verdicts currently cached. Each avoids a whoami call to Synapse.

panels.title: Thumbnails without generating
panels.description: Share of thumbnail requests answered from Synapse's store or the worker's cache, with no decode and no trip to Synapse.

panels.title: Request rate by endpoint
panels.description: Which endpoints the worker is actually taking.

panels.title: Response status
panels.description: 404 is routine for media. 401 means tokens are being rejected; 503 means Synapse could not be reached to validate one.

panels.title: Latency by endpoint (p95)
panels.description: Downloads are dominated by file size; thumbnails by whether one had to be generated.

panels.title: Thumbnail outcomes
panels.description: The panel worth watching. synapse_store and worker_cache are free; generated costs a decode; proxied means the worker could not do it at all. A healthy server is mostly the first two, with generated tapering as caches warm.

panels.title: Thumbnail generation time
panels.description: Generation is CPU-bound and bounded by media.max_concurrent_thumbnails. If p99 climbs while CPU is idle, requests are queueing for a slot.

panels.title: Thumbnail write-through
panels.description: Thumbnails written into Synapse's own media store. Any 'failed' means the worker fell back to its own cache; check the logs for why.

panels.title: Proxied back to Synapse
panels.description: Requests the worker declined. unsupported_format and animated are expected; anything else is worth investigating.

panels.title: Uploads/sec
panels.description: Media accepted and stored by the worker.

panels.title: Bytes in/sec
panels.description: Throughput of accepted uploads.

panels.title: Rejected/sec
panels.description: Uploads refused for a reason the spec defines. Routine at low rates; a spike in 'limited' means a client is leaking pending media IDs, and 'over_quota' means media_upload_limits is biting.

panels.title: Failed/sec
panels.description: Uploads the worker could not complete. Should be zero.

panels.title: Proxied/sec
panels.description: Handed to Synapse, i.e. accept_uploads is off.

panels.title: Media IDs reserved
panels.description: Async uploads started via /_matrix/media/v1/create.

panels.title: Uploads by endpoint and result
panels.description: endpoint and result are separate dimensions: sync, create and async are endpoints; stored, reserved, too_large, limited, over_quota, forbidden, conflict, not_found, failed and proxied are outcomes.

panels.title: Upload throughput
panels.description: Bytes written to the media store on behalf of local users.

panels.title: Federated fetches
panels.description: Media the worker downloaded from other homeservers itself. 'failed' falls back to proxying, so it degrades rather than breaks.

panels.title: Upstream requests
panels.description: Dispatch across the Synapse media workers. An uneven split with least-connections usually means one worker is slow, not that balancing is broken.

panels.title: Upstream in-flight
panels.description: Requests currently being served by each Synapse worker. Persistently high means the pool is too small.

panels.title: Access token validations
panels.description: 'accepted' includes cache hits, so this is not the whoami call rate. 'error' means Synapse could not be asked, which surfaces as 503 rather than a rejection.

panels.title: Token cache size
panels.description: Bounded by auth.max_entries. At the limit, the least recently used verdicts are evicted and revalidated.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: Cores used. Thumbnail generation is the only CPU-heavy path.

panels.title: Resident memory
panels.description: Decoding holds the whole bitmap, so this tracks concurrent thumbnail generation more than request volume.

panels.title: Goroutines
panels.description: Roughly one per in-flight request.

panels.title: Open file descriptors
panels.description: Each served file holds a descriptor for the length of the transfer.
